clue.text: Very emotional, pull back before going with girls? About right

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next one in the answer
pulling something back turns it to face the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to pull is to tug

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the short piece sits inside the longer phrase

parts.note: wenching is an old word for chasing or consorting with young women
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man's emotional confession: he pulls back before chasing girls, and wonders whether that's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull back' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'back' acts alone on 'pull'. Wenching is a dated word for womanising.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gut-wrenching is so distressing it is felt physically, hence intensely emotional.

clue.text: Twice soak turned up as buddy of yesteryear

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music and numbering
to sog is to soak

explanation.surface: Getting drunk twice turns a person into an old drinking buddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossib is an obsolete form of gossip in its old sense of a close friend or godparent.

clue.text: Swimming, terrapins give off water vapour

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Terrapins swimming about release moisture into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants and skin transpire by passing moisture out through pores as vapour.

clue.text: Colourless county town that's shunned by a ramble

indicators.note: the word by itself is shunned, so those letters are removed

parts.note: wan means pale
Derby is the traditional county town of Derbyshire

explanation.surface: A dull county town is avoided by walkers on a ramble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'by' after 'shunned' is the very word removed from DERBY.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander is to stroll aimlessly, much as a ramble is a leisurely walk.

clue.text: Burundi parched with earth in coarse state

parts.note: RU is the international vehicle code for Burundi

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the other word

parts.note: parched means dry
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Burundi, dry and earthy, is described as a rough place.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudery is the condition of being rude, crude or vulgar.

clue.text: Ancient Scandinavian stag that was nursing antler's tip

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: stag is an old word for an informer, and a nose is a police informer

indicators.note: a tip is an end, here the last letter of the word

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An old Viking stag shelters a broken antler tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That was' marks an obsolete sense: a stag once meant an informer, as does nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse means relating to ancient or medieval Scandinavia and its people.

clue.text: Solar hat, at being doffed, muddled Alice

indicators.note: doffed means taken off, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters removed

indicators.note: muddled means confused, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Confused Alice takes off her sun hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliac is a rare synonym of heliacal, meaning relating to or near the sun.

clue.text: Greeting not applicable with teacher leaving last

indicators.note: the last letter leaves, so the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: N/A is the abbreviation for not applicable
a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A greeting is no longer needed once the teacher has left last of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Namaste is the Hindu salutation made with palms pressed together.

clue.text: Unconventional part of dodgy psychology

indicators.note: part of means only a piece of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Unorthodox thinking is dismissed as a bit of dubious psychology.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across dodGY PSYchology.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, the word suggests a free, nomadic, bohemian way of living outside convention.

clue.text: Scottish supernumerary joining the men with the Gunners

indicators.note: with simply sets one piece alongside the next in sequence

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, the ordinary soldiers
RA is the Royal Artillery, whose soldiers are gunners

explanation.surface: A spare Scottish soldier is attached to an ordinary unit serving alongside the artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: Military abbreviations: OR for other ranks, RA for the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Orra is a Scots adjective meaning odd or extra, an unattached spare person or thing.

clue.text: Plants with edible shoots? A thousand such will achieve fame

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Japanese plants of the aralia family whose young shoots are eaten

definitions.text: A thousand such will achieve fame
definitions.meaning: second reading: put K, a thousand, in front of the word and you get a word for fame

explanation.surface: A grower muses that a thousand such vegetable plants would make them famous.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: K (a thousand) plus the answer makes KUDOS, meaning fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Udo is an East Asian herb, Aralia cordata, grown as a vegetable for its blanched young stems.

clue.text: Dealt blows with king trapped, make frequent quick moves

indicators.note: trapped means caught inside, so one letter goes within the others
blows as in blows up, scattering the letters

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A boxer traded punches with a king pinned against the ropes, darting about.
explanation.definitionFit: To dartle is to dart repeatedly, a frequentative form of the verb.

clue.text: Eastern Belarus providing home for a mass sales market

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern

indicators.note: to provide a home for something is to house it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: BY is the international vehicle code for Belarus
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eastern Belarus is said to host a huge marketplace for mass selling.
explanation.walkthrough: E then BY with A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: eBay is the online auction site where millions of items are bought and sold.

clue.text: Palms swaying round brown N. Indian? Source of illumination within (12, two words)

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the mixed letters go outside the other pieces
swaying things move about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
tan is a light brown colour
the Dards are a people of the north of the Indian subcontinent

explanation.surface: Swaying palms surround a brown-skinned northern Indian, as in a tropical scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dards are a hill people of Kashmir and the north-west. 'Within' in the definition means indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard lamp is a tall floor-standing lamp used to light a room indoors.

clue.text: Some person deployed as high-altitude weather forecaster

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the answer is a run of letters inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Somebody is sent up high to act as a weather forecaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across perSON DEployed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonde is an instrument sent aloft on a balloon or rocket to measure atmospheric conditions.

clue.text: Bug when producing glimmer etc?

parts.note: a bug is a hidden microphone, MIC for short
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which bug makes a faint glimmering light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glimmer' is an old name for mica; 'etc' and the question mark turn it into a plural class.
explanation.definitionFit: Glimmer is an archaic term for mica, and the plural covers the whole group of these shiny silicate minerals.

clue.text: Bill adjusted in hotel group? It swells irritatingly

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other word

parts.note: a hotel chain is a group of hotels under one owner

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A guest's bill was altered at a chain hotel, which irritatingly inflates it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilblain is an itchy, swollen inflammation of the skin caused by cold.

clue.text: Introduced trend is what opens exhibition possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

indicators.note: what opens a word is its first letter

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A new fashion trend is launched at the opening of an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert something is to put it in, so introduced and inserted are synonyms.

clue.text: Temple entrances prince with foreign king shown round close to one

indicators.note: shown round means displayed surrounding, so this word wraps the next pieces

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for prince
roi is French for king
on can mean next to, as a town on a river
a means one

explanation.surface: A prince and a foreign king are given a tour of a temple near one of its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: The French king surrounds the 'close to one' pieces, which go in just after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronaoi is the plural of pronaos, the porch or vestibule in front of a classical temple's inner chamber.

clue.text: Mineral identifying office location, we hear

indicators.note: we hear points to what is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the offices is an old euphemism for the lavatory, so its location is the site of the loo

explanation.surface: Identifying a mineral by where an office is located sounds odd but is reported second-hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' (usually 'the offices') is a dated British euphemism for the lavatory, a loo.
explanation.definitionFit: Leucite is a white or grey potassium aluminium silicate found in volcanic rocks.

clue.text: Let off without what'll go with peas by the sound of it

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or without

indicators.note: by the sound of it means as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: the phrase mind your p's and q's pairs the letter p with q

explanation.surface: Someone is spared the duty of serving the peas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peas' is said like P's, and P's go with Q's in the idiom about good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to release them from an obligation or let them off a penalty.

clue.text: Feel effects of drug law — it's tough but transparent

parts.note: to trip is to experience a hallucinogenic drug
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A drugs law is described as tough yet clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests strict but transparent legislation; the definition is the safety glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Triplex is a trade name for laminated safety glass, strong yet see-through.

clue.text: Alkali underwent examination in spring welling up

indicators.note: in a down clue welling up means rising from the bottom, so it is read upwards
in places one word within the other

parts.note: to spring is to hop
to have sat an exam is to have undergone it

explanation.surface: An alkali was tested in water bubbling up from a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is potassium carbonate or a related potassium compound, a strongly alkaline substance.

clue.text: S'poses (not a genuine word) Bill has been swallowed by snake!

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so this piece goes into the other

parts.note: a seps is a kind of venomous snake of classical legend
a bill is an advertising poster, AD for short

explanation.surface: A man supposes, using a made-up word, that someone named Bill has been eaten by a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition flags a ghost word: SEPAD is a Scots dialect form for 'suppose' rather than a standard word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepad is a dialect form of suppose, so the third person sepads matches the colloquial s'poses.

clue.text: Coloured glass like this is filled with liquor

indicators.note: filled with means the second word goes into the first

parts.note: so means in this way
malt is malt whisky

explanation.surface: A coloured glass like this one is filled with spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalto is coloured glass or enamel used in mosaic work.

clue.text: Commission taking HM north of the border?

indicators.note: in a down clue north of means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: Her Majesty is the monarch, ER for Elizabeth Regina
a rand is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A task sends the Queen up into Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' suggests Scotland, but here it puts the HM piece above a word for border.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a task one is sent to do, as an errand is.

clue.text: Trouble and strife? Such courage is artificial

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rhyming slang for wife
second meaning: the bravery that comes from drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble and strife' is Cockney rhyming slang for wife, and 'my old dutch' is another Cockney term for her. Courage bottled from alcohol is the false kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch is Cockney slang for a wife, and Dutch courage is the boldness induced by drink.

clue.text: Christmas time to adorn mostly with what glows

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to deck is to adorn, as in decking the halls
an ember is a glowing piece of coal

explanation.surface: At Christmas one decorates with things that glow, like fairy lights or candles.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas falls in the last month of the year, so that month is the season of Christmas.

clue.text: A day's march? Five running in helmet — a pest

indicators.note: a run of five consecutive letters sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: five letters run across the end of the first word and the next two words

explanation.surface: On a day's march, a pest gets inside a soldier's helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five' tells you the length of the run: helmET A PEst.
explanation.definitionFit: An étape is a stage of a journey, the distance marched by troops in one day, or the halt at its end.

clue.text: University reduced, then scrapped, scarcely old

indicators.note: reduced means cut to its short form, here an abbreviation

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: something scrapped is broken up, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A university was cut back and then closed altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' in the definition marks an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneth is an obsolete adverb meaning with difficulty, hardly or scarcely.

clue.text: Harvest brought back and left inside, not so fresh

indicators.note: brought back means returned the way it came, so it is read backwards
inside places one letter within the other word

parts.note: to reap is to harvest
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Produce harvested, brought home and left lying around is no longer so fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Paler means more washed out or faded, losing the bright colour that freshness implies.

clue.text: Pastry dish, one filled with a mixture of spices and fish paste

indicators.note: filled with means other letters are put into the middle of this word

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish
taken as written
masala is an Indian spice blend
a means one

explanation.surface: A recipe for a pastry dish with a spicy filling and a fish paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the final A, added after the filled pastry; the other A goes inside with the spice mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Taramasalata is a Greek dip or spread made from fish roe, bread or potato and oil.

clue.text: Pets set out for a short walk in India?

indicators.note: out means removed, so these letters are taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to cosset is to pet or pamper
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Pet owners in India take their animals out for a brief walk.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove SET from COSSETS. The question mark warns that the coss, about two miles, is short only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A coss is an Indian unit of distance of roughly one to three miles, so a walk measured in it.

clue.text: Lines facing leader gave tongue in poetic mode

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the opinion page set opposite the editorial, or leader
second meaning: a poetic past tense of a verb used of hounds starting to bay

explanation.walkthrough: A leader is a newspaper editorial; 'gave tongue' is what hounds do when they open, or begin to bay, on a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: An op-ed is an opinion column opposite the editorial page, and ope is poetic for open, so oped means opened.

clue.text: Light baked crust can, with ace filling

indicators.note: filling means going into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a can is a tin
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A cook bakes a light crust in a tin, with an ace filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tian is a Provençal gratin of layered vegetables baked with a light crust, named after its dish.

clue.text: Ocean 'bouilli' done with lots of spices

parts.note: the high seas are the open ocean

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A boiled-beef dish, bouilli, cooked at sea with plenty of spice.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouilli is boiled meat; here the French word for boiled works as the anagram signal.
